narrative.text: The distribution arrives not at your office but at an intermediary's address in the Amber Coast — the same shell company through which you originally invested in Vael's Thornfeld Opportunity Trust. The Lytheiran bank that serves as the intermediary reports that the fund has performed as projected: your 5,000 ₭ is now 15,000 ₭, held in an account registered to a holding company that is registered to another holding company that is registered to a nominee director whose name appears on three dozen similar entities. On paper, you do not exist. The money does. The trail, if anyone were to follow it, goes through two jurisdictions and ends at a law firm that does not answer questions. But trails can be followed. Banks can be compelled. Shell companies can be pierced. The question is not whether the structure is perfect — no structure is perfect. The question is whether anyone is looking.

The distribution has been processed through the agreed channels. The Lytheiran intermediary confirms the funds are available for transfer to any jurisdiction you designate — or they can remain in place, reinvested in the next fund cycle. I should note, Chancellor, that the Bureau of Civic Accountability has recently made inquiries about offshore financial arrangements involving senior government officials. My fund is not currently a subject of those inquiries. Whether it becomes one depends, in part, on whether anyone provides them with reason to look. I am not suggesting anything. I am observing that discretion remains the better part of wealth preservation.

The money is offshore, hidden behind two shell companies and a nominee director. If the BCA is active — if Nadia Voss is investigating — this is exactly the kind of structure she was trained to unravel. She prosecuted twelve Halvek-era officials and won every case. She knows what shell companies look like. She knows which banks ask which questions. The 15,000 ₭ is real, but so is the risk: the moment someone starts pulling on the thread of Vael's fund, my name — or rather, the shell company registered to my intermediary — is part of the fabric. I can collect the money and move it deeper. I can leave it offshore and hope no one looks. Or I can close the position now, return the capital, and hope the trail goes cold before anyone follows it.

choices.text: "Transfer the 15,000 ₭ back to Veltria — through another intermediary, routed as a foreign investment return from a Lytheiran portfolio. The money comes back clean: taxes paid, source documented as a generic offshore fund, nothing traceable to Vael or the Thornfeld Trust. My family's accounts receive a legitimate-seeming investment return from a foreign portfolio. If anyone asks, I invested in a Lytheiran diversified fund before taking office and it matured. The story is simple, defensible, and difficult to disprove without access to Lytheiran banking records — which the BCA does not have and will not get. Do it carefully. Do it once. And close the shell companies afterward."

"Leave the money offshore. Do not transfer it. Do not touch it. The 15,000 ₭ stays in the Lytheiran account, reinvested through the same structure, earning returns in a jurisdiction where no one is asking questions. I do not need the money in Veltria. I need the money to exist — somewhere safe, somewhere quiet, somewhere I can access if I ever need it. That day may come. If this government falls, if the BCA becomes a weapon against me rather than a tool of accountability, if I need to leave the country and start over — the money will be there. It is not greed. It is insurance. Chancellors who do not plan for the possibility of failure do not survive failure."

"Close everything. Liquidate the position. Return the original 5,000 ₭ to my personal accounts through a legal repatriation — pay whatever taxes are owed, file whatever disclosures are required. The 10,000 ₭ profit goes to the Veltrian Treasury as a voluntary contribution, with a public statement that I am returning investment gains from a fund whose membership I can no longer justify. I do not name the fund. I do not name Vael. I simply state that I have discovered an investment that created an appearance of conflict and I am resolving it. The shell companies are dissolved. The Lytheiran accounts are closed. The trail goes cold — not because it is hidden, but because it ends in voluntary disclosure. That is the difference between concealment and correction. I am correcting."
